# Chih-Yu Lin

## The right information, at the right time

How can wireless networks support sensing, inference, control, and decision-making under strict timeliness and resource constraints? I develop **learning-based resource allocation** methods that determine *what* information a task needs, *when* it should be refreshed, and *how* limited radio, sensing, computing, and energy resources should be shared.

## Selected work

::: {.selected-grid}
::: {.selected-card}
[![](images/System_Architecture.png){.selected-thumb fig-alt="System model for the NOMA-ISCC vehicular network"}](research.qmd)

<p class="selected-meta">IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · 2026</p>

### Keeping safety-critical information fresh in vehicular networks

A computation-aware NOMA-ISCC framework that jointly schedules sensing, communication, and computation — so vehicles act on information that is still fresh when it arrives.

[Read more →](research.qmd)
:::

::: {.selected-card}
[![](images/IntercellInterference1.jpg){.selected-thumb fig-alt="Cell-edge multicast groups facing inter-cell interference in a multi-cell NOMA network"}](research.qmd)

<p class="selected-meta">IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · 2024</p>

### When larger multicast groups beat interference — and when they don't

Reveals the trade-off between multicast group size, inter-cell interference, and information freshness in multi-cell NOMA, with a provably optimal AoI-aware scheduling strategy.

[Read more →](research.qmd)
:::

## Open to collaboration

I am actively looking for collaborators on:

- **Freshness- and task-aware networking** — Age of Information, task-oriented and semantic metrics, scheduling theory
- **ISAC and vehicular networks** — predictive beamforming, cooperative multi-RSU sensing, vehicular communication systems
- **Learning-based resource allocation** — reinforcement learning and transformer-based control for 6G networks

If your research intersects with any of these directions, I welcome the opportunity to discuss potential collaboration.

## Background

Before my Ph.D., I worked as an engineer at TSMC and ASMedia, on semiconductor design workflows and high-speed USB4 IP solutions. This industry experience shapes how I approach wireless systems research: with attention to implementation constraints, not only theoretical performance.
